- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward modestly.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (e.g., +10%+ above recent high); cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.0% downward bias in next forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out abrupt changes by averaging last 3–5 forecast points.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00s), model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid “overbought” trap.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mid-range stability; anchor forecast near 20-day moving average of history.
